compiled_by: Agent J (from combined Agent B/C/D data + historical remediation throughput rates)

completion_model.scope: Bring all 38 Domain E seeds from Unprocessed/Archived → Certified

scenario_1_sprint.name: Sprint (Aggressive — Minimal Governance)
scenario_1_sprint.description: All 38 seeds remediated in 3 large batch runs. Pack C and Pack D EW authoring done in parallel by separate agents. Pre-written COSO EW templates for common control concepts. CC audit done concurrently with Wave 1. Assumes CC discrepancies resolve quickly (single-object confirmed).
risks: CC discrepancies may take longer than planned
Parallel agents may introduce concurrent-write conflicts (DL-019 pattern)
Reduced per-item quality review may produce lower-quality EW text
Governance guard batch cap forces minimum 2 batches (38 items / 28 = 2 batches)

milestones.day_1_afternoon: Wave 2 (12 items Core Concepts) + Wave 3a (7 items Core CAs)
milestones.day_2_morning: Wave 3b-c (9 items IT Controls) + Wave 4 (7 items Capstone)

scenario_2_standard.name: Standard (RECOMMENDED — Balanced Governance)
scenario_2_standard.description: Sequential Pack C then Pack D, 4-wave execution with independent per-batch verification. Each wave completed and governance-verified before next wave begins. CC audit completed before any EW authoring. EC enhancement done during certification pass (not as separate pre-pass).
risks: Sequential execution is slower but eliminates concurrent-write risk
Independent verification per batch adds ~30 min but catches defects early
CC audit may uncover architecture issues that require plan adjustment

milestones.day_1: CC audit (resolve 5 discrepancies). Wave 1 (4 items Foundation) — both packs.
milestones.day_2: Wave 2 (12 items Core Concepts). Wave 3a (7 items Core CAs).
milestones.day_3: Wave 3b-c (9 items IT Controls). Wave 4 (7 items Capstone).
milestones.day_4: EC enhancement pass. DL-031 recalibration. CAQS six-dimension verification. Governance sign-off.

scenario_3_conservative.name: Conservative (Maximum Safety — Full Audit First)
scenario_3_conservative.description: Full architecture audit on all 38 seeds first (single-object vs dual-block). CC verified by two independent agents. Then EW authoring with per-item quality review. EC enhancement pass before EW authoring (EC quality dictates EW topic alignment). DL-031 recalibration before certification. Two-agent sign-off on every certification decision.
risks: Overly conservative timeline delays Domain E closeout
May be unnecessary if CC audit confirms single-object architecture quickly

milestones.week_1: Full architecture audit. CC verification. EC enhancement pass (17 items).
milestones.week_2: EW authoring in 4 waves with per-batch verification. DL-031 recalibration.

critical_path.bottleneck: EW Authoring (53 slots across 38 items) — 2-3 days
pre_requisites: Archived seeds unarchived to Unprocessed for authoring

completion_impact.note: After all 38 seeds certified, 241 items remain to reach 100% certification across all 5 packs. Remaining: Pack A partial B/C/F, Pack C sections C-F, Pack D sections C/E/F, Pack E Section C.

completion_model.recommendation: Scenario 2 (Standard) — 3-4 working days. Balances governance compliance with throughput. Sequential execution avoids DL-019 concurrent-write risk. Per-batch verification catches defects early.

notes: Completion model uses historical remediation throughput rates from S805 (25 items in ~3 hours with pre-written templates) and DL-026 autonomous runs (27+17 items in ~2 hours enforced-depth). EW authoring without pre-written templates is slower (10-15 items/day). The 53 empty EW slots are the dominant cost driver. If pre-written COSO EW templates are prepared before execution, the Standard scenario can compress to 2-3 days.
